info.title: PetShop API
info.description: ## About PetShop **PetShop** is an online marketplace for pet owners. In one place, customers can buy food, toys and accessories for their pets from independent stores, and find trusted grooming, veterinary and training centers nearby. The platform brings four kinds of users together: * **Customers** browse the catalogue, compare products by pet type, brand and price, pay at checkout and follow every order until it is delivered. * **Vendors** open their own store, manage products and stock, process orders and withdraw their earnings. * **Service providers** present their center with a price list, team, weekly schedule and photo gallery. * **Administrators** approve new sellers and centers, moderate reviews and manage the site content. PetShop is a full-stack web application: a React website on top of this API. The API stores the data, enforces the business rules (stock, prices, order statuses, approvals, permissions) and powers every page of the website. Live website: [pet-shop-frontend-side.vercel.app](https://pet-shop-frontend-side.vercel.app) **Built with:** Java 17, Spring Boot 3, Spring Security (JWT), PostgreSQL, Liquibase, OpenAPI / Swagger. ## What the API covers | Area | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Storefront** | Product catalogue with search, filters, sorting, best sellers, stores, service providers, blog | | **Buyer** | Cart, wishlist, checkout, order tracking, addresses, reviews | | **Vendor** | Own store, products and stock, received orders, sales dashboard, finance and payouts | | **Service provider** | Center profile, price list, team, weekly schedule, gallery, visitor metrics | | **Admin** | Seller approval, catalogue and site content, orders, payouts, coupons, review moderation | ## How to try it 1. Open **Auth** and run `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (or register a new account). 2. The returned token is applied automatically, so locked endpoints work right away. You can also paste it manually with the **Authorize** button. 3. Open any section, choose an endpoint, press **Try it out**, then **Execute**. Endpoints with a lock need a signed-in user; the others are public. Use the selector at the top to show one audience only (storefront, vendor, provider, admin). ## Roles | Role | Can do | | --- | --- | | `BUYER` | Shop, check out, track orders, write reviews | | `VENDOR` | Manage own store, products, orders and payouts | | `SERVICE_PROVIDER` | Manage own center, services, team and schedule | | `ADMIN` | Approve sellers, manage content, oversee orders and payouts | Vendors and service providers start as `PENDING_APPROVAL`. They can sign in and prepare their store, but can publish only after an admin approves them. ## Main flow 1. Vendor registers → admin approves → vendor adds products. 2. Buyer adds products to the cart → checks out (stock is reserved, one order per store). 3. Vendor moves the order **pending → processing → shipping → delivered**. 4. Buyer reviews the product → its rating updates. 5. Service provider registers → admin approves → the center is listed and services can be published. ## Status codes | Code | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `200` / `201` | Success / created | | `400` | Invalid input; field errors are listed in `data` | | `401` | Not signed in, token expired or wrong credentials | | `403` | Wrong role, not the owner, or account waiting for approval | | `404` | Resource not found | | `409` | Conflict: duplicate, not enough stock, invalid status change | | `429` | Too many requests (login, forms) |
